items.item: Car Share Text Amendment (N 100284 ZRY)
items.outcome: CPC approved with modifications 2010-08-11; City Council adopted Res 0470-2010 on 2010-09-29.
items.notes: Citywide text, so there is no CB6-specific ZAP record. The conditions come from the friendly amendment in the minutes and CB6's letter (reproduced in the CPC report).

conds.c: Car-share spaces not to exceed 20% of total spaces in any one parking facility
conds.e: The adopted text caps car share at 'five spaces or 20 percent ... whichever is greater' in accessory residential facilities (R5-R10), 10% in R3-2/R4, but allows 'up to 40 percent' in public parking facilities.

conds.c: Car-share spaces must not reduce the number of spaces required to be reserved for building occupants
conds.e: The CPC noted CB6's comment 'that car share vehicles should not be allowed to park in required residential parking spaces' and answered that 'car share vehicle parking spaces will serve a population that includes the same people for whom the required accessory parking is intended'; the text lets car share use required accessory spaces, subject to the caps and a plaque/30-day request right.

items.item: 341 10th St (Prospect Towers) rezoning R6A/R6B to R7-3/C2-4, MIH, LSGD special permits incl. parking reduction (C 230337 ZMK, N 230338 ZRK, C 230339 ZSK, C 230340 ZSK, N 230341 LDK)

items.notes: The applicant told CPC that 'all rent stabilized residents with parking spaces today will maintain those spaces'. That is an applicant statement, not a City condition.

conds.c: Tie rezoning to an ironclad CBA protecting current tenants and ensuring number and permanent affordability of new HPD units and existing units

However, an Article XI regulatory agreement was signed with HPD in July 2024: 'long-term affordability with income restrictions for all 154 units' of the existing building. No signed CBA document was found.

conds.c: Do not waive/reduce the parking requirement

items.item: 41 Richards St rezoning M1-1 to M1-5 (C 230051 ZMK)
items.outcome: CPC approved 2024-03-20; Council adopted 2024-04-18; no mayoral veto
items.notes: Unconditional approval.

items.item: City of Yes for Economic Opportunity citywide text amendment (N 240010 ZRY)
items.outcome: CPC approved with modification 2024-03-06; Council adopted with modifications 2024-06-06; no mayoral veto
items.notes: The last five conditions are the board's support for SBIDC positions; they endorse parts of the proposal rather than restrict it. Verdicts are based on the CPC report text and the Council's summary of modifications, not a full read of the adopted text.

conds.c: Restrict home-occupation business hours to 7am-6pm
conds.e: Neither the CPC modifications (1,000 sf cap, explicit hazards, no common-area use) nor the Council modifications ('Reduce allowance to only 1 employee', 'Maintain current prohibition on animal-related businesses') include operating hours.

conds.c: Permitted uses must not conflict with quiet enjoyment of residences
conds.e: CPC added 'fire, explosions, toxic and noxious matter, radiation, and other hazards' to the home-occupation restrictions. Council: 'Strengthen performance standards to address noise, vibrations, and exhaust concerns'.

conds.c: Life sciences/medical labs in residential areas capped at 10,000 sf unless in a hospital/medical center
conds.e: Council: 'Prohibit labs in C1-1 through C1-4 overlays outside Manhattan'. This is stricter in those overlays but is not the requested size cap.

conds.c: Minimum floor-plate size that triggers separate egress stairs in mixed commercial/residential buildings
conds.e: Not found among CPC or Council modifications reviewed.

conds.c: Full mitigation of environmental nuisances into residential portions of mixed-use buildings
conds.e: Council (Proposal 5): 'Strengthen performance standards to address noise, vibrations, and exhaust concerns'; 'Require that amusement uses always be located below, not above, residential units'; 'Prohibit rooftop bars above residential apartments'.

conds.c: Home occupations limited to three people incl. owner(s) and employees
conds.e: Council: 'Reduce allowance to only 1 employee (as is currently permitted)'. This is stricter than the board asked.

conds.c: BSA approval of auto repair must bar repairs, petroleum use and charging on any public way/sidewalk
conds.e: Council: 'Prohibit all auto repair uses in C1 districts' and 'Strengthen BSA special permit for light auto uses in C2-C7 districts, with a focus on concentration effects'. CPC: 'use of streets, sidewalks, public plaza space remain illegal except where expressly permitted by DOT'. No explicit public-way finding was added.

conds.c: Micro-distribution: off-sidewalk bike parking/storage and storefront transparency
conds.e: Transparency comes through Proposal 12 streetscape rules (CPC: 'require transparency for active uses'). Bike-delivery requirements are 'beyond the jurisdiction of zoning' (CPC). Council added a 'BSA special permit for micro-distribution centers in C1 and C2 districts outside Manhattan'.

conds.c: (SBIDC-aligned) Allow new uses in commercial zones: small-scale production, micro-distribution, life sciences, live entertainment, amusements
conds.e: Adopted, but the Council added size caps and exclusions, e.g. 'Establish size limits of 3,000 square feet in C1-1 through C1-4 overlays'. Labs are prohibited in C1-1 to C1-4 outside Manhattan, and micro-distribution needs a BSA permit in C1/C2 outside Manhattan.

conds.c: (SBIDC-aligned) Allow amusements & entertainment on commercial corridors
conds.e: Proposal 10 adopted with size limits (3,000/5,000/10,000 sf by district). Proposal 9 nightlife/dancing had no zoning modification.

conds.c: (SBIDC-aligned) Update loading requirements to enable adaptive reuse
conds.e: Proposal 4 ('Modernize loading dock rules') had Council modifications: 'None'. CPC called it 'appropriate'.

conds.c: (SBIDC-aligned) Fix bulk rules for film studios etc.; 40 ft straight box without setback
conds.e: Proposal 17 created a bulk-waiver authorization 'in line with the loft building envelopes established for the new C7 and M districts' (CPC). Council: 'Ensure reasonable limitations to the scope of authorization'. No 40 ft straight-box rule found.

conds.c: (SBIDC-aligned) Update Use Group classification system
conds.e: Proposal 6 (NAICS-based use classification) had Council modifications: 'None'.

items.item: Red Hook Coastal Resiliency city map amendments & acquisitions (C 240035 MMK, C 240036 PQK)
items.vote: 26-0-3 per minutes (CB letter says one abstention); ZAP marks the rec 'Received after Clock Expired'
items.outcome: CPC approved 2024-05-01; Council adopted 2024-06-20 (no modifications); no mayoral veto

conds.c: Update the data behind design decisions to reflect current flooding reality
conds.e: CPC defended the existing design basis without changing it: 'The project accounts for 30 inches of sea level rise, which is the NPCC's high (90th percentile) estimate for sea level rise in the 2050s ... A higher level of protection would require higher built interventions'.

conds.c: Do not exclude the large buildings, small businesses and supermarket at the end of Van Brunt St
conds.e: CPC: 'the alternative outermost alignment ... could provide protection to a greater number of properties ... However, this alternative was not pursued because it did not meet FEMA HMGP funding criteria'. It noted only that the project protects 'three electrical sub-stations which serve these waterfront sites, including the site of a supermarket'.

conds.c: Regular, active community engagement and consultation
conds.e: CPC: 'The Commission is also pleased that DDC plans to engage in robust community engagement throughout construction'. This is a stated plan, not a binding condition.

items.item: 150 Mill St rezoning M1-1 to M1-5 (C 220080 ZMK)
items.vote: 28-2-2 per CPC report; no count in minutes; ZAP marks the rec 'Received after Clock Expired'
items.outcome: CPC approved 2024-07-24; Council adopted 2024-09-26 (no modifications); no mayoral veto
items.notes: The Borough President recommended disapproval. CPC called required industrial space 'outside the scope' but 'encourages the applicant to work with local industrial service providers'.

conds.c: Applicant and local CBOs prepare a letter or MOU outlining the CBA's inclusions
conds.e: CPC did not address the CBA/MOU. Council Res. 586 'approves the Decision of the City Planning Commission' with no conditions. Commercial Observer (Sept 2024) reports only that 'Pilku promised to lease most of the building to light manufacturing tenants' and mentions no CBA or MOU. A private MOU may exist; none was found.

conds.c: Applicant continues dialogue with local CBOs through ULURP
conds.e: CPC hearing summary: 'The applicant team provided an overview of their correspondence with tenants of the NYCHA Red Hook Houses ... discussed their conversations with stakeholders in the area'. The dialogue happened, but it was not a City condition.

conds.c: CB6-sponsored community task force (floor amendment)
conds.e: No record found in later CB6 minutes or City documents.

items.item: City of Yes for Housing Opportunity citywide text amendment (N 240290 ZRY)
items.vote: 34-0-2 (ZAP/CB letter). The minutes file fb/2024-06-06-full-board.txt shows the motion but no count.
items.outcome: CPC approved with modification 2024-09-25; Council adopted with modifications 2024-12-05; no mayoral veto
items.notes: Unconditional. The CB letter: 'We still hope for a more comprehensive planning process but are happy to support and approve COY in its entirety.'

items.item: 176 Dikeman St bulk authorization ZR 75-21 for film studio (N 250270 ZAK)
items.vote: 32-0 per CB letter text (ZAP disposition fields: 33-0-0)
items.outcome: CPC approved 2025-11-05 (authorization, no Council review)

conds.c: Increased street-wall transparency around the set fabrication shop
conds.e: The CPC post-referral review deck (10/20/2025) restates the condition but shows no response. No CPC report was found (cpc/250270.pdf returned 404).

conds.c: Install rooftop solar array
conds.e: NYCEDC press release (Oct 8, 2025) on the two Echelon studios: 'over 25 percent of electric demand expected to be supported by rooftop solar panels'. This is a documented plan, not a CPC condition, and the statement covers both facilities.

items.item: 46 Nelson St rezoning M1-1 to M1-2A/R7A & M1-2A/R6A (MX-5) + MIH (C 250094 ZMK, N 250095 ZRK)
items.outcome: CPC approved 2026-04-01; Council adopted with modifications 2026-05-14 (removed MIH Option 2, added Option 3); no appeal
items.notes: The Council's MIH modification ('remove MIH Option 2 and add Option 3') was not a CB6 condition.

conds.c: Applicant agrees the building will be constructed as currently designed
conds.e: A zoning map amendment does not bind design. The only restrictive declaration covers an 'LPC-approved construction protection plan'. Council Res. 477 approves the map with no design conditions.

conds.c: Reduce studios; add more 2- and 3-bedroom units
conds.e: CPC: 'the Commission appreciates that the applicant has modified the unit mix to include more three-bedroom units in the proposed development, based on direct feedback from the Community Board.' Hearing summary: 'an overall reduction in the number of studios and the addition of 12 three-bedrooms.' This was done voluntarily by the applicant; CPC called it 'outside the purview of the Commission'.

items.item: 175 Third St (Gowanus): transfer of development rights from Powerhouse Arts landmark + bulk & WPAA authorizations (N 260141 ZAK, N 260142 ZCK, N 260143 ZCK, N 260145 ZAK, LDKs)
items.vote: 28-3-2 (CB letter dated 3/13/2026 refers to the 'March 12, 2026' meeting)
items.outcome: CPC approved 2026-04-01 (certifications/authorizations; no Council review); CPC letter 2026-08-19
items.notes: Related: on 2025-09-10 CB6 approved as presented the Powerhouse Arts continuing maintenance plan needed for the landmark transfer (LPC matter, fb/2025-09-10-full-board.txt).

conds.c: Powerhouse Arts promenade opened to the public as a direct result of the development-rights transfer
conds.e: The recorded Continuing Maintenance RD with the Powerhouse Arts condo board (OCR'd, 24 pp.) has no public-access provision found. The Waterfront RD grants a 'perpetual and non-exclusive public access easement' over the 175 Third St WPAA/PAA, not over Powerhouse's own waterfront. Only the first 30 of its 340 pages were OCR'd. No CPC report was found.

conds.c: 30% of the 1,071 units affordable, averaging 60% AMI (MIH Option 1)
conds.e: Brownstoner (Apr 2026): 'About 250 apartments will be set aside as affordable housing under Mandatory Inclusionary Housing, triggered by the Gowanus rezoning', about 23% of units. No added affordability was found tied to the CPC actions.

items.item: City of Yes for Carbon Neutrality citywide text amendment (N 230113 ZRY)
items.pos: Approved (per CB6's own June 2024 CoY Housing letter: 'We've now approved all three portions (Carbon Neutrality, ...)')
items.outcome: CPC approved 2023-09-11; Council adopted with modifications 2023-12-06
items.notes: ZAP's BK CB6 disposition has no recommendation or vote filled in, and no vote appears in the fb/ minutes. Included for completeness only.

gowanus.outcome: CPC approved C 210177 ZMK with modifications on Sept 22, 2021 (signature page: nine commissioners, Larisa Ortiz abstaining); CPC modifications moved the taller Parcel 4 tower south with a 125-ft northern tower for the Thomas Greene pool shadow and let waterfront remediation/excavation proceed early. Council Land Use Committee voted 18-0-0 on Nov 10, 2021 to modify N 210178 ZRK (struck MIH Option 2, raised Gowanus Mix incentive to 0.3+0.3 FAR, narrowed the Mix use list, added Mix recording/monitoring, lowered heights south of Thomas Greene to 125 ft); CPC found no further review needed Nov 17, 2021. Council adoption recorded 2021-11-23 (ZAP milestone; ZR adoption date 11/23/2021); Brownstoner reports 50 in favor, Menchaca the lone no. Mayoral review milestone 2021-11-30. The POA contains 56 commitments (~$250M plus ~$200M NYCHA). As of 2026-09-24 the Task Force tracker shows 10 Completed, 23 Progressing on Schedule, 16 Progressing with Delays, 5 Stalled (incl. Gowanus Green housing, remediation, park and school), 2 Not Started.

earlier.sum: Approved BSA variance for Whole Foods (UG6 >10,000 sf in M2-1 at 3rd St/3rd Ave) with conditions: follow-up traffic study after one year, 10pm closing, storefront treatment. Vote 31-3-0. Project-by-project stance under existing manufacturing zoning.

earlier.pos: Lightstone 363-365 Bond St: conditional approval; motions to have CPC table applications failed
earlier.sum: Committee motion asking CPC to table Lightstone renewal/minor modification until SEIS, 30% affordable, 8 stories, and RDP compliance failed 10-26. Scotto motion asking CPC to 'table all applications in regards to the development along the Gowanus Canal until they hold true to their commitment to move forward with the rezoning and EIS of the entire Gowanus corridor' failed 18-17-2. Levine motion approving with conditions (DCP full-scale corridor rezoning study, CB6 Responsible Development Policy, new EIS) passed 27-4-6.

earlier.pos: General support for Bridging Gowanus framework
earlier.sum: 36-0-2: support for 'guarantee investments in sustainable infrastructure', a new Gowanus Manufacturing Zone, a new 'Mandatory Mixed Use Zone', affordable housing, 'pathway to responsible growth'; include CB6 Responsible Development Policy in any zoning plan; friendly amendment adding no noxious uses incompatible with residential and active street facades.
Land use committee minutes record 'considerable skepticism' about citywide MIH (AMI accuracy, displacement, payment-in-lieu) as it would apply to future Gowanus/4th Ave rezonings.

Letter dated May 7, 2019 asks DCP to 'adopt options 1 and 3' for MIH, make City-owned sites '100% affordable', 'synchronize infrastructure upgrades with project development', states 'a commitment to NYCHA is central to a positive view of this exercise', proposes a NYCHA FAR bank, periodic re-evaluation (~7 years), and a Park/Environmental Improvement District; calls Gowanus Mix 'vague'.

Requested DCP changes for long-time businesses at Bond/4th St incl. exempting 413 Bond St from waterfront access and visual corridor (30-0-1); supported Old American Can Factory envelope re-evaluation without increased FAR to keep affordable arts space in the Gowanus Mix (32-0-0); tabled transit FAR-bonus motion before formal review (35-0-1).
29-0-0 to support Gowanus CAG request to DEC to reclassify canal from Class SD to Class I.

conds.c: City support and fund a Gowanus Zoning Commitment Task Force with quarterly public meetings, City updates, and a dedicated NYCHA liaison
conds.e: POA #1: 'Support the Council, Community Board 6, and other stakeholders to form a Community Oversight Task Force' ... 'Quarterly meetings will be open to the public' ... representation incl. 'NYCHA'. Tracker 1.1 status: Completed.

conds.c: City finance a Task Force facilitator for 15 years plus independent professional planning expertise for the same period
conds.e: POA #1: 'The City and City Council are assisting in identifying independent resources for this facilitator' and 'City agencies will dedicate staffing resources through the end of 2037'. No commitment to City-funded facilitator or planning expertise.

conds.c: Every five years, a full City assessment of FEIS adverse impacts and whether mitigations worked
conds.e: POA #1: 'Every five years, 2027, 2032, 2037, DCP will prepare a community update report on plan implementation, housing and economic development, and population and demographic data' (not framed as an FEIS mitigation assessment).

conds.c: Task Force uses CB6 Responsible Development Policy to review projects; developers report on RDP categories
conds.e: No provision found in the POA, CPC report or Council modification summary.

conds.c: EPA written review of the City's CSO projections
conds.e: EPA issued written comments dated Aug 9, 2021 on the DEIS; per the Sept 8, 2021 Velazquez/Simon letter: 'EPA has identified significant and substantive inconsistencies in the City's wastewater and stormwater calculations in Chapter 11 and Appendix F of the DEIS.' (Review delivered by EPA, and it was critical.)

conds.c: City fully comply with EPA order to complete CSO retention tanks on EPA-mandated timeline
conds.e: POA #44: 'While the City will comply with the Order, it must ensure that the specific milestones are feasible and will continue to discuss those issues with the EPA.' Tracker 7.6: Progressing on Schedule.

conds.c: Unified Stormwater Rule in effect before the first site sewer connection in the rezoning area
conds.e: POA #39 applies USWR to 'all new development that discharges to sewers in the rezoning area'; 'DOB will provide DEP, the Council Members and CB6 a monthly list of all building permit applications submitted ... before the USWR is in effect' (monitoring, not a hard gate). Tracker 7.1: Completed.

conds.c: Continual CSO modeling/monitoring, per-connection modeling, reporting to community and Task Force
conds.e: POA #41: 'the City will prepare an annual report on applicable project approvals and completions ... anticipated sanitary discharge, development site storm flow ... Data will be made publicly available'; POA #40 CSO solids monitoring plan submitted to EPA.

conds.c: Final EIS must study dry-weather sewage capacity from Gowanus to Red Hook plant via underground viaducts
conds.e: FEIS text not reviewed; CPC report restates the request but does not say whether FEIS added the analysis.

conds.c: Public Place: continued EPA review and EPA conclusion that remediation is compatible with residential/school/park uses
conds.e: POA #9 quotes EPA Aug 9, 2021 letter: 'EPA believes that it is feasible for the site to be cleaned up to allow for the types of land uses currently under consideration' and EPA/NYSDEC 'agreed to work cooperatively'. No final EPA compatibility determination; tracker 3.2 (remediation) Stalled.

conds.c: EPA review of individual brownfield development applications before permitting
conds.e: No such commitment found. POA quotes EPA: 'NYSDEC generally has the lead on the upland cleanups along the Canal'.

conds.c: Make the Gowanus Mix mandatory rather than an incentive
conds.e: Council kept the incentive model and enlarged it: 'the incentive would be increased to 0.3 FAR ... and 0.3 FAR for the inclusion of Gowanus Mix defined uses, bringing the total floor area bonus to 0.6 FAR'; adds 'a recording and monitoring requirement for Gowanus Mix uses'.

conds.c: Weight specific Gowanus Mix uses and require a percentage of artist/light-manufacturing space to be permanently affordable
conds.e: Council modifications refined the use list (removed several use groups, added UG 17B) but no affordability requirement is described.

conds.c: Arts: protect existing studios, require new subsidized arts space, designate a share of Gowanus Mix for arts and culture
conds.e: Council modification removed 'UG 12 commercial art galleries, jewelry and art metal craft shops' from the Mix; POA's only related item is #56 'EDC will promote the Industrial Developer Loan Fund'. No arts set-aside described.

conds.c: Encourage and expand material re-use / sustainable industry cluster
conds.e: POA #32: DEP 'commits to reestablish permanent facilities for each operation [DSNY, Big Reuse, GCC] on site in the final design'.

conds.c: MIH: mandate Option 3 (Deep Affordability) with Option 1; Options 2 and 4 unacceptable
conds.e: Council: 'The Potential Modifications would strike MIH Option 2, leaving MIH Option 1 and the Deep Affordability Option.' Adopted text (11/23/2021) lists 'APPENDIX F ... (Option 1, Deep Affordability Option)'. CPC had approved Options 1, 2 and 3.

conds.c: Community preference extended equally to CDs 2, 6, 7, 8, 9, plus a preference for public housing residents
conds.e: No POA item. First rezoning-area lottery (420 Carroll St, Aug 2024): 'Preference for 20 percent of the units will be given to residents of Brooklyn Community District 6.'

conds.c: City fund an independent racial-impact study before public review concludes
conds.e: A racial equity report by Columbia's Lance Freeman was released Aug 2021; per Urbanize, Fifth Avenue Committee 'helped fund the study'. No evidence the City funded it.

conds.c: All MIH affordable units on the same zoning lot as market-rate units; equal amenity access
conds.e: Not addressed in CPC report or Council modification summary; adopted MIH text not checked for off-site provisions.

conds.c: Additional housing types: transitional, foster-care youth, artist set-asides, artist live/work
conds.e: POA #8 Gowanus Green: '~115 units ... for seniors, approximately 73 units ... supportive housing' (already in plan); nothing on foster youth, transitional or artist housing found.

conds.c: Commit to translating the Gowanus IBZ Vision Plan into zoning; interim mechanism to curb detrimental uses
conds.e: POA #27 commits only to 'continue engaging' and that DCP 'will also consider the Gowanus IBZ as part of any broader initiative to revise and update industrial zoning'. (Later delivery not checked.)

conds.c: $5M open-access broadband conduit system in the IBZ
conds.e: POA #22: DoITT outreach to franchisees; City 'will explore the feasibility of coordinating broadband conduit work ... pending funding availability, public conduit.' No $5M. Tracker 5.1: Progressing with Delays.

conds.c: IBZ streetscape/transit commitment comparable to ENY $8.2M; 3rd Ave mobility study 9th St-Hamilton; loading zones every IBZ block
conds.e: POA #25: 'DOT commits to a study of 3rd Avenue from 9th St to Hamilton Avenue/16th Street' incl. loading zones; 'Funding: $500,000 expense.' Tracker 5.4: Not Started.

conds.c: Detailed plan and grants (up to $50K, Greenpoint model) for displaced businesses incl. Salt Lot
conds.e: POA #15: 'SBS will create a Gowanus Business Grant Program ... Each business will be eligible to receive grants of up to $50,000 per business.' Tracker 4.2: Progressing on Schedule.

conds.c: Workforce: $350K/yr for 10 years (Stronger Together model), 18-25 NYCHA industrial training, fill NYCHA REES coordinator
conds.e: POA #19 '$250,000 annually' FY2023-2027; POA #26 industrial job training 'ages 18-25, particularly NYCHA residents' '$200,000 annually' FY23-FY25; POA #20 '$605,000 annually'. Shorter than 10 years; REES position not mentioned.

conds.c: Local sourcing of goods and services by new businesses/developments
conds.e: No commitment found.

conds.c: Firm plan for early-childhood program capacity (incl. children with disabilities)
conds.e: CPC: FEIS identified 'significant adverse impacts with respect to community facilities (publicly funded child care services)'; no POA item; FEIS mitigation chapter not reviewed.

conds.c: Identify and set aside at least one additional school site beyond Public Place
conds.e: POA offers a notification mechanism instead (#54: 'DOB will notify the SCA, DOE, and affected Community Board when an owner/developer files plans'); only the Gowanus Green school (#53) is committed, tracker 9.3 Stalled.

conds.c: Full assessment of health care, fire and police service impacts
conds.e: No evidence found either way.

conds.c: Investments in senior services (health care, senior centers)
conds.e: No POA item found.

conds.c: Capital commitment and timeline for Public Place / Gowanus Green park
conds.e: POA #30: 'Funding: $14.4M capital'; timeline 'To be determined based on finding an alternative location for EPA Staging'. Tracker 6.3: Stalled.

conds.c: Thomas Greene Playground: mitigate pool shadow; capital commitment/timeline; temporary park and pool during remediation
conds.e: CPC modified text 'to require the taller of the two towers be located on the southern portion ... northern tower ... 125 feet'; Council lowered heights south of the playground 145→125 ft; POA #29 City to ensure 'access to comparable facilities, including a public pool'. Timeline tied to Superfund; tracker 6.2 Progressing with Delays.

conds.c: Capital commitment and timeline for Head of Canal (Head-End CSO) park
conds.e: POA #31: 'DEP confirms that the open space at the Head End site will be completed in late-2030.' Tracker 6.4: Progressing on Schedule.

conds.c: Additional open space on City/MTA lots (Salt Lot, GreenSpace on 4th, F/G Transit Plaza, Under the Tracks), mapped as parkland
conds.e: POA #32 Salt Lot open space 'following community engagement'; POA #33 request MTA release parcel 'north of 9th Street' for a promenade ($5.9M if successful); no parkland-mapping commitment; GreenSpace on 4th and Under the Tracks not named.

conds.c: Create a Parks Improvement District funded by assessment on new development
conds.e: POA #28: 'The City will support community efforts to create a Gowanus Waterfront Business Improvement District (BID)'. Tracker 6.1: Progressing on Schedule.

conds.c: Consider permanent street closures for open space
conds.e: POA #48 Nevins Street improvements 'may include an open street or shared street activation'; tracker 8.2: Stalled.

conds.c: Fund flood study of IBZ and Red Hook, update it, report to Task Force, and commit capital
conds.e: POA #42: DEP 'commits to including the rezoning area, Gowanus IBZ and Red Hook neighborhood' in cloudburst vulnerability assessment; POA #43 sewer upgrade 'Funding: $174M capital'. Tracker 7.4 Progressing with Delays; 7.5 Progressing on Schedule.

conds.c: Capital for a Gowanus community preparedness plan (Ready Red Hook model)
conds.e: No POA item found.

conds.c: Require urban heat island strategies in the Special District and WAP
conds.e: Not found in CPC or Council modification summaries.

conds.c: Fully fund ~$274M NYCHA capital need at Gowanus Houses and Wyckoff Gardens with concrete plan and dedicated liaison (the stated precondition)
conds.e: POA #3: 'the City will allocate approximately $200M in capital' for in-unit renovations. Brownstoner: 'the $200 million is less than the $274 million NYCHA estimated is needed'. Tracker 2.1: Progressing with Delays.

conds.c: Resident inclusion and accountability in capital work, with mandatory regular reporting
conds.e: POA #4: 'NYCHA will hold meetings quarterly'; 'third-party facilitator and/or independent technical advisor, selected by residents and contracted by NYCHA'. Tracker 2.2: Progressing with Delays.

conds.c: NYCHA work to follow HUD Section 3 local hiring
conds.e: POA #4 lists 'Section 3 job opportunities' as a discussion topic with residents; no hiring requirement stated.

conds.c: Update transit analysis beyond the 2010 traffic-zone baseline and propose achievable mitigation
conds.e: Not checked in FEIS.

conds.c: MTA/NYCT confirm two extra northbound AM-peak F trains are feasible before approval
conds.e: No evidence found.

conds.c: Work with MTA to restore the B71 bus
conds.e: No POA item found; later MTA action not checked.

conds.c: Make Union St R station accessible; prioritize accessibility at peripheral F/G stations
conds.e: CPC: 'the transit bonus Chair certification, which is unique to the original application, will still apply' for Union Street station improvements; no City commitment to fund elevators.

conds.c: Update pedestrian/traffic safety analysis for Open Restaurants
conds.e: No evidence found.

conds.c: Assess bicycle impacts and identify bike safety infrastructure
conds.e: POA #47 mentions 'bike racks' among possible streetscape elements only.

conds.c: Expand and enforce loading zones throughout the rezoning area
conds.e: POA #25 study will 'evaluate the broader IBZ to improve loading zones' (IBZ only, not the rezoning area).

conds.c: Water access at Head of Canal, Salt Lot, Gowanus Green; emergency egress between every bridge
conds.e: CPC: CB6's request 'for the designation of specific locations for particular amenities within the zoning text itself is not feasible'. POA #38: City 'will explore potential in-water access at two City-controlled locations: Gowanus Green and the 2nd Ave street end by the Salt Lot'. Tracker 6.11: Progressing with Delays.

conds.c: WAP to facilitate pedestrian bridges (1st St Basin, Degraw St, Gowanus Green-Salt Lot)
conds.e: POA #35: DOT navigation study 'upon completion of the Superfund work'. Tracker 6.8: Not Started.

conds.c: Waterfront programming funded/overseen via the Parks Improvement District
conds.e: POA #28 BID 'focused on stewardship, access, and public programming of open spaces, including new and existing waterfront esplanades'.
